clue.text: Mug smashed after use

definitions.note: mug is slang for the face, the whole set of facial parts

indicators.note: something smashed is broken into pieces, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A cup gets broken once it has been used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed' rearranges the eight letters of AFTER USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mug is slang for face, and one's facial looks are collectively one's features.

clue.text: Small town dropout

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters of the word before it are put out of order

explanation.surface: A small town that gets left behind by people who drop out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropout' reads as one word, but it splits into DROP and the anagram signal 'out', which rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dorp is a South African word for a village or small country town.

clue.text: "Hot water's here!", said the bloke

indicators.note: said tells us the word for a bloke is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: geezer is British slang for a man, a bloke

explanation.surface: Someone announces the hot water is ready, as reported by some man.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a GEYSER is also a gas water heater over a sink or bath, so hot water comes from it; GEEZER is slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural hot spring that spouts, or in Britain a household water heater, is where hot water comes from.

clue.text: One leaving a deep impression

parts.note: reads as someone memorable, but literally describes a craftsperson who cuts lines deeply into metal or wood

explanation.definitionFit: An artisan who incises designs into a surface literally leaves cut impressions in it.

clue.text: Hoisting this, the builder strained a ventricle

definitions.note: a builder hoists a projecting beam into place

indicators.note: strained suggests something pulled out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A builder lifting a heavy beam overexerts himself and damages his heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strained' rearranges A VENTRICLE; the heart-strain picture hides an extended definition describing the beam a builder hoists.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a projecting beam supported at one end, the sort of heavy member a builder lifts into position.

clue.text: Here people aren't treated well

parts.note: reads as a complaint about bad service, but means a place where people who are not well get treated

explanation.definitionFit: A medical centre where outpatients who are unwell receive treatment.

clue.text: Fragrant tree, old and at heart gnarled

indicators.note: gnarled means twisted and knotted, so the letters are twisted into a new order
at heart takes the central letter of the word and

explanation.surface: An old knotted tree gives off a pleasant scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' takes N, the middle of 'and'; 'gnarled' then rearranges TREE, OLD and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent means strongly scented, a direct synonym of sweet-smelling.

clue.text: Former Archbishop left in anger almost

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for left within the shortened word for anger
almost drops the final letter of the word for anger

parts.note: temper is a synonym of anger

explanation.surface: A former archbishop departed in something close to a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TEMPER to TEMPE and 'in' puts L inside. William Temple was Archbishop of Canterbury in the 1940s.
explanation.definitionFit: William Temple, and his father Frederick, were both Archbishops of Canterbury.

clue.text: Almost night!

parts.note: reads as dusk approaching, but a word for close by is spelt like night with its last letter missing, and that word means almost

explanation.walkthrough: NIGH, a synonym of the answer, is 'night' lacking its final letter: almost night.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly and nigh both mean close to or almost, and nigh is very nearly the word night.

clue.text: When full, it marks the end

definitions.text: When full, it marks the end

parts.words: When full, it marks the end
parts.note: reads as something brimming over at a finish, but describes the punctuation mark called a full one that ends a sentence

explanation.definitionFit: A full stop is the punctuation point placed at the end of a sentence.

clue.text: Helpers disguised as Martians

indicators.note: disguised means changed in appearance, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Kindly volunteers dressed up as aliens from Mars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised' rearranges AS MARTIANS. The Samaritans is a British charity offering help to people in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Samaritans are helpers, after the Good Samaritan of the parable who aided a stranger.

clue.text: Trollope was one sounding more proper

indicators.note: sounding tells us the word for more proper is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: righter means more correct or proper

explanation.surface: The Victorian novelist Anthony Trollope apparently spoke rather correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Trollope was a Victorian novelist; RIGHTER and WRITER sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope was a prolific Victorian novelist, an example of an author.

clue.text: Embroidered cloths showing exotic striptease

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and unusual, so the letters take an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: Decorated fabrics depict a rather racy dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges STRIPTEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapestries are woven or stitched wall hangings, decorated textiles.

clue.text: Poet who was nothing to doctor

parts.note: love is zero, nothing, in tennis scoring
to doctor a drink is to lace it, adding something secretly

explanation.surface: A poet who meant nothing to the physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb here, as in spiking a drink. Richard Lovelace was a 17th-century Cavalier poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Lovelace was an English Cavalier poet who wrote To Althea, from Prison.

clue.text: This soldier appears strange without one

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd, so the letters are rearranged
without means the letters of one are left out of the rearrangement

parts.note: a is one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A soldier looks odd when alone or without a mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges APPEARS and 'without' removes A (one), leaving the six letters of a military engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapper is a military engineer, a soldier who digs trenches and lays or clears mines.

clue.text: PO11 could be written on its front

definitions.text: PO11 could be written on its front

parts.words: PO11 could be written on its front
parts.note: PO11 looks like a code, and is a Portsmouth-area postcode, the kind of thing written on the outside of a letter cover

explanation.walkthrough: British postcodes such as PO11 (a Portsmouth area) go in the address on the front of mail.
explanation.definitionFit: The paper cover of a letter carries the address, postcode included, on its front.

clue.text: The front-seat passenger is so determined

definitions.meaning: a passenger is conveyed in a car by someone else at the wheel

explanation.surface: A determined person riding beside the driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Driven means highly motivated, and a passenger is carried along by the motorist.

clue.text: Piece of gold found in the patisserie

definitions.meaning: a former French twenty-franc gold coin
a layered puff pastry with cream filling, like a mille-feuille

explanation.surface: A gold coin discovered in a French cake shop.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both an old French gold coin and a layered cream pastry.

clue.text: Drop handkerchief in river

indicators.note: in places the cloth within the river name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain, flowing through Chester and Aberdeen
a rag is a piece of cloth, a makeshift handkerchief

explanation.surface: Someone lets a handkerchief fall into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' is a noun, a small sweet or lozenge, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragee is a sugar-coated sweet, the kind of small lozenge also called a drop.

clue.text: Don't observe this festival

definitions.meaning: to ignore or overlook something, failing to notice it
the Jewish spring feast commemorating the Exodus

explanation.surface: An instruction to ignore a particular religious holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass over is to overlook; Passover is the Jewish festival recalling the Exodus.

clue.text: Help given by Ruth once in the field

definitions.text: given by Ruth once in the field
definitions.meaning: Babe Ruth was a baseball star; a fielder credited with helping to put a runner out is credited with this

explanation.surface: Ruth helped out with the harvest long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' suggests the biblical gleaner in the fields, but it is Babe Ruth, the American baseball player.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help; in baseball an assist is a fielding throw leading to a putout.

clue.text: Band set off in two directions

indicators.note: in places the word for set off between the two compass points

parts.note: S and E are south and east, two compass directions
to trip an alarm is to set it off

explanation.surface: A band of musicians departed heading two ways at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' means a strip of colour, not musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a long narrow band of colour or material.

clue.text: Smart club in super refit

indicators.note: in puts the playing-card abbreviation inside the rearranged letters
refit means rebuilt, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A stylish golf club gets a fine overhaul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refit' rearranges SUPER into SPRUE, and 'in' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce means neat and smart in appearance.

clue.text: One who makes a lot of signs

definitions.text: One who makes a lot of signs

parts.words: One who makes a lot of signs
parts.note: reads as a sign-painter or someone gesturing, but refers to the twelve zodiac signs and a horoscope-caster

explanation.definitionFit: A horoscope reader works with the zodiac signs constantly.

clue.text: Target of thirsty Archers? Nonsense!

definitions.meaning: a bullseye is the archers' target, and in the radio soap The Archers the village pub is named this

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of archers looking for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap set in the village of Ambridge, whose pub is The Bull.
explanation.definitionFit: The bull is the centre of an archery target and the Ambridge pub; bull also means nonsense.

clue.text: Poet excluded from audition

indicators.note: from audition says the word for excluded is heard rather than seen, giving a same-sounding word

explanation.surface: A poet is kept out of a casting call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' suggests a casting session, but means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bard is a poet, especially in old Celtic tradition, and Shakespeare is the Bard.

clue.text: Please turn out

indicators.note: turn means to change position, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A polite request for someone to switch off the lights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn out' looks like one phrase, but 'turn' is the anagram signal on PLEASE and 'out' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone out cold or out for the count is sleeping or unconscious.

clue.text: Busy cottagers have no time for French food

indicators.note: busy suggests bustling activity, so the letters are stirred up
have no means the letter for time is left out of the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Hard-working villagers have no spare moments for fancy foreign cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy' rearranges COTTAGERS and 'have no' removes one T (time), leaving the letters of a snail dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargots are snails cooked as a delicacy in French cuisine.
